item.title: UMG, Roblox agree strategic partnership to expand music integrations
item.description: Universal Music Group (UMG) and gaming platform Roblox have announced a new strategic agreement aimed at expanding music, merchandise and commercial integrations across artist and fan experiences. Under the agreement, the two companies will collaborate on tools designed to increase engagement and revenue opportunities for artists and labels on Roblox. item.title: Major sponsors back 9th AFRIMA awards set for Lagos in January
item.description: The Lagos State Government, First Bank of Nigeria, Guinness Nigeria and several other public and private sector organisations have been confirmed as sponsors of the 9th edition of the All Africa Music Awards (AFRIMA), scheduled to take place in Lagos from 7 to 11 January 2026. item.title: Fela Kuti to receive Lifetime Achievement Award at 2026 Grammy Awards
item.description: The Recording Academy has announced that Afrobeat pioneer Fela Anikulapo Kuti will be honoured with a Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2026 Grammy Awards, recognising his enduring impact on global music and culture. Kuti will be recognised alongside fellow honourees Whitney Houston, Chaka Khan, Cher and Paul Simon. item.title: UK: Roger Faxon steps down from Salt board
item.description: Roger Faxon has stepped down from his role at British music technology company Salt after contributing to its strategic direction and growth, the company has confirmed. item.title: Hybe partners Tyla in strategic move into African music market
item.description: South Korean entertainment company Hybe has entered into a partnership with Grammy Award-winning South African singer Tyla, marking a strategic move into the African music market rather than a change in the artist’s management structure. The partnership was announced on 15 December, prompting speculation that the 23-year-old artist had changed management. item.title: Kenyan court clears producers’ Skiza Tune royalties case against Safaricom
item.description: The High Court of Kenya has ruled in favour of five music producers, allowing them to proceed with a lawsuit against telecommunications firm Safaricom over alleged unpaid royalties from the Skiza Tune caller ring-back service. The decision marks a significant step in ongoing disputes within Kenya’s music industry concerning transparency and accountability in royalty collection and distribution. item.title: Suno adjusts AI music ownership terms after Warner Music partnership
item.description: Suno has outlined planned policy changes for 2026 that will place greater emphasis on subscriber-only monetisation and revise how ownership of AI-generated music is defined, following its recent agreement with Warner Music Group (WMG). item.title: Condolences pour in for renowned Ghanaian drummer, composer Paa Kow
item.description: Internationally acclaimed Ghanaian drummer and composer Paa Kow has reportedly died on 23 December 2025, prompting an outpouring of tributes from musicians and cultural figures in Ghana and beyond. The cause of death has not yet been disclosed. The news was announced by American jazz trumpeter Brad Goode, a long-time collaborator, in a Facebook post. item.title: Gunna announces African dates following $15 Million North American tour
item.description: Despite concerns over rap’s ability to fill venues and a slip in the genre’s 2025 sales share, American rapper Gunna has reported strong commercial results from his Wun World Tour, grossing nearly $15 million and selling roughly 200,000 tickets across 18 North American shows. item.title: Spotify’s 1000-stream threshold criticised by Southeast European indie labels
item.description: A recent study by the Association of Independent Music Publishers and Producers Bulgaria (ANMIP-BG) has raised concerns that Spotify’s 1000-stream threshold is negatively affecting nearly two-thirds of independent artists and labels in Southeast Europe, particularly those with large back catalogs. The Spotify policy, which requires a track to reach 1000 annual plays before generating royalties, has drawn criticism for potentially excluding smaller or niche artists from fair compensation.
